title: Event (PublicEvent)
description: A committed public fact with a stable cursor. Rust: crates/agentscope-durable/src/types/commit.rs::PublicEvent. Java: DurableTypes.PublicEvent. Field naming note: the wire field for the event kind is `type` (Rust #[serde(rename = "type")]); this document also knows it as `kind` in prose. `required`/extension semantics come from core's JournalEvent (crates/agentscope-core/src/journal/event.rs): namespaced kinds such as durable/finalization_started are required extension events, so a reader that does not know their codec must stop recovery.

schemaVersion.description: Envelope version written by append_event. Core journal envelopes are version 2 (JournalEvent::SCHEMA_VERSION); this is the durable public-event envelope and is a separate counter.

eventId.description: Stable identity of the fact. Re-appending the same id with different content is rejected as CONFLICT ('Event identity changed').

sequence.description: Per-session monotonic counter, rendered as a decimal string (u64 in Rust). Session-scoped, so sequence 1 of two sessions are different facts.

cursor.description: Opaque page cursor: '<session storage key>:<sequence>'. Requests pass it back verbatim; a cursor below the pruned watermark answers cursor_expired and the client resyncs from snapshot.

data.description: Event payload; for turn status events it is {"status": TurnStatus, "revision": n}.

KnownKind.description: Kinds the durable backend itself commits, plus the namespaced required extension events the agentscope adapter registers. Host-defined kinds are admitted by the second branch of EventKind.

EventKind.description: The event kind. The enum half names every kind this repository writes; the string half admits a host-defined kind, which the durable runtime allows as long as it does not start with a reserved prefix (session./thread./run./step.).

anyOf.$comment: Host-defined kind. Commit.event types are rejected when they start with session./thread./run./step.; namespaced kinds (e.g. durable/…) are extension events and may be `required`.
